discovery: Controlled/living radical polymerization (atom transfer radical polymerization, ATRP), enabling precise synthesis of well-defined functional polymers
rationale: Recent Chemistry prizes have gone to biochemistry (2024 protein design) and materials (2025 MOFs). That makes a core synthetic-methods or polymer-chemistry prize plausible for 2026. ATRP is one of the most widely used methods in modern polymer science, with very large citation impact and broad industrial use. Matyjaszewski (Wolf Prize 2011) and Sawamoto each discovered it independently in 1995, and the pair has long been named in Nobel forecasts. Close alternatives are next-generation DNA sequencing (Balasubramanian, Klenerman) and solid-phase DNA synthesis (Caruthers).
